outline: Risk, assessment, risk management and risk governance have become key concepts in modern society's attempts to manage environmental and health problems connected with human activities and products. The object of this course is to train an integrated interdisciplinary understanding of environmental risks and their management by perspectives and approaches from natural and social sciences. This course also critically examines the role of risk assessment in environmental management by checking the methods used, as well as the underlying theories and assumptions.
schedule:
1st week- General Introduction
2nd & 3rd weeks- Introduction to environmental health risk assessment  and Management
4th & 5th weeks- Hazard identification and dose–response assessment
6th week- Formulating the Problem
7th and 8th weeks- Assessing the Risk
9th week- Appraising the Options
10th week- Addressing the Risk
11th week- Cross-Cutting Aspects of Risk Management
12th week- Midterm exam
13th week- Environmental Impact Assessment
14th & 15th weeks- Case Study
16th & 17th weeks- Final report
18th week- Final exam
